key_insight: An agentic LLM system can turn complex TCGA clinical data into accurate natural-language answers by using specialized tools, not just a larger model.
clinical_relevance: This could make oncology data analysis faster and more accessible for researchers by supporting auditable, clinically contextualized queries over large cancer datasets.
method: ReAct-style LLM agent chooses from 8 tools for extraction, statistics, survival analysis, hypothesis testing, and verification
Benchmarked on TCGA-Agent-Bench with 440 queries across 5 difficulty tiers
Compared against rule-based, single-pass LLM, and retrieval-augmented baselines
evidence_signal: The system reached 93.4% overall accuracy and outperformed a rule-based pipeline (87.1%), single-pass LLM (81.8%), and RAG (66.9% on a 50-query subset).
watch_item: Performance depends on tool coverage and curated reference data, so gaps in source fields or tool errors could limit reliability.
paper_title: A ReAct Agentic AI System for Natural Language Querying and Statistical Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
